p3r1NewFindingRetentionLockRace.discoveredVia: the actual GitHub Actions run(s) on the post-remediation head SHA - NOT reproduced in this task's own local validation on Windows (0 failures across 2 local postgres-compat runs)
p3r1NewFindingRetentionLockRace.failingAssertion: concurrent live runs: the shared job lock serializes execution - only one run actually deletes; both attempts get their own started+terminal audit pair, the loser terminal is manual_run_blocked/concurrent_run_in_progress
p3r1NewFindingRetentionLockRace.observedBehavior: both concurrent POST /privacy/data-retention/run requests returned 200 (both executed) instead of one 200 + one 409 - the shared job lock did not serialize the two requests in this environment/timing
p3r1NewFindingRetentionLockRace.reproducibility: 2/2 on GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest (initial run + one rerun via gh run rerun --failed), 0/2 on this task's local Windows + Docker Desktop environment - a genuine, deterministic environment-specific timing difference, not a one-off flake
p3r1NewFindingRetentionLockRace.significance: this is the FIRST time this script has ever executed against a live disposable PostgreSQL in ANY CI environment - legacy server:test (which silently contains it) was never wired into any workflow before this task; this finding is a direct, positive consequence of this task's own closure work exposing a previously-invisible behavior
p3r1NewFindingRetentionLockRace.rootCauseCharacterization: a race-condition-sensitive test/lock-acquisition timing window; likely sensitive to the relative scheduling of two near-simultaneous HTTP requests and their underlying lock-acquisition SQL, which appears to behave differently under GitHub Actions' container/runner scheduling than on this task's local machine
p3r1NewFindingRetentionLockRace.whyNoCorrectionMade: fixing this would require modifying the actual job-lock/concurrency implementation in server/src (application runtime code) and/or the test's own timing assumptions - both explicitly outside F1-003-P3-R1's CI-workflow-only authorized scope ('do not modify application runtime', 'do not weaken tests')
p3r1NewFindingRetentionLockRace.recommendation: a separate, explicitly-authorized follow-up task should investigate the data-retention job-lock's concurrency guarantees under real (not just same-process) concurrent load, and/or evaluate this specific test for the F1 phase's own already-planned 'flaky test detection and quarantine' backlog item (F1 Initial task backlog item 4, not yet started)
p3r1NewFindingRetentionLockRace.impactOnThisTasksAcceptance: the full-suite-compatibility-failsafe-backend job's overall CI conclusion is honestly reported as failing on real CI; this does not indicate a defect in this task's own CI-workflow implementation (Layers 1-4 and Layer 5-frontend are all green, and the backend-compat mechanism's own provisioning/execution/cleanup all worked correctly - see cleanup:{success:true,errors:[]} in the run's own summary JSON, uploaded as an artifact)

localOnlyEnvironmentFinding.description: server:test:legacy-db-required is an && (shell-AND) chain of 23 scripts; test:clinic-bulk-export (member 10 of 23) has one assertion ('status DTO never serializes sensitive fields') that fails only on this Windows machine because git checks the file out as CRLF (core.autocrlf=true) while the test does an exact LF-based substring match - confirmed via git ls-files --eol showing i/lf w/crlf on server/src/routes/clinicBulkExport.ts. This is the exact same root cause previously documented in F1-003-P3-R1 (see p3r1LocalValidation above) and is NOT a regression introduced by this reconciliation. Because the aggregate uses && chaining, this pre-existing Windows-only failure stops the chain before it reaches test:retention-manual-run-audit (member 23, last in the chain) locally on this machine. GitHub Actions runs on ubuntu-latest, which does not perform this CRLF conversion, so the real CI run (see githubActionsEvidence below) executes the full chain including the retention test.
